item.title: With hope of being 'the last team standing,' Cubs seek to even series vs. Reds
item.description: With the regular season winding down, the Chicago Cubs hope to find some consistency and momentum as they look to even their three-game series against the host Cincinnati Reds on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: With the regular season winding down, the Chicago Cubs hope to find some consistency and momentum as they look to even their three-game series against the host Cincinnati Reds on Saturday night. The Cubs (85-69) dropped the opener 6-4 on Friday. They erased a 2-0 hole and turned a 3-2 deficit into a 4-3 advantage for their only lead of the game, but a three-run sixth by Cincinnati put Chicago behind again for good. The Cubs entered the series having taken two of three games from the National League East-leading Atlanta Braves. Chicago is tied for the first NL wild-card spot with the Philadelphia Phillies and San Diego Padres. Yet despite their struggles of late -- the Cubs have lost three of their past five games -- they haven't lost their belief. "I don't think we've ever lost sight of what our potential is. We still feel like we can absolutely be the last team standing," designated hitter Michael Conforto said earlier this week. "Regardless of what the standings say or what's going on in the division, it doesn't change the fact that we feel like we can win the rest of the series through the end of October." The Cubs have eight games remaining, including series against the Miami Marlins and Boston Red Sox to close the season. Capitalizing with men on base will be one area where Chicago will look for better results on Saturday. The Cubs went 2-for-10 with runners in scoring position on Friday. Trailing 2-0 in the second, they cut the deficit in half and then had the bases loaded with one out and Pete Crow-Armstrong and Seiya Suzuki next at the plate. But Reds starter Chase Burns struck both out to retire the side. Matthew Boyd (8-5, 4.16 ERA) will start for the Cubs on Saturday. The left-hander is 2-3 with a 6.32 ERA in six career starts against Cincinnati. The Reds (72-82) will counter with Nick Lodolo (3-5, 5.12 ERA) as they look to take the series. Lodolo is coming off his longest outing of the season, going seven innings and taking the loss in a 4-1 setback against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Monday. The lefty, who hasn't won a start since July 5, is 2-2 with a 4.53 ERA in 10 career starts against the Cubs. Cincinnati is eyeing its first series victory since earlier this month, when it won two of three games against another division foe, the majors-leading Milwaukee Brewers. It was the Reds' third straight series triumph, which began with taking two of three games against the Cubs in Chicago. On Friday, with the bases loaded in the sixth inning, Jose Trevino delivered a single that drove in JJ Bleday and Eugenio Suarez to put the Reds ahead 6-4. Suarez's hit two batters earlier allowed Elly De La Cruz to tie the game at 4-4. "Just take the moment for what it is, whether you succeed in it, great. If you fail in it, it's ok, you learn from it," said Trevino, 33. "Been in plenty of those situations my whole career. I tend to gravitate to, and like, those situations. I don't know why." --Field Level Media

item.title: グリーンランド合意、トランプ氏「勝者」を演出との見方－対立収束へ
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米国とデンマーク、グリーンランドは、グリーンランドで米国の関与を拡大する安全保障協定で合意した。デンマーク自治領のグリーンランドの領土を米国に譲り渡すことなく、長期化していた外交対立はいったん収束する。

トランプ米大統領は18日、米国がグリーンランドの安全保障について「恒久的な管理権」を持つことで合意したと明らかにした。デンマークとグリーンランドの首脳も、ニューヨークで22日から始まる国連総会の一般討論に合わせて協定に署名する見通しだと確認した。

協定の詳細はまだ公表されていない。デンマークのフレデリクセン首相は、協定がデンマーク王国の「主権と領土の一体性」と、グリーンランド住民の自決権を認めるものだと説明した。トランプ氏がグリーンランドの所有権や主権を得る内容ではないことを示唆している。

これは、グリーンランドを米国の支配下に置く、あるいは米国領にすることを目指してきたトランプ氏の従来の主張から大きく後退した内容だ。領土取得を繰り返しトランプ氏が要求したことで、米国と欧州の同盟国の間では不信感が高まり、北大西洋条約機構（NATO）内にはここ数十年で最も深刻な亀裂が生じていた。

デンマーク国防大学戦略・戦争研究所のマーク・ヤコブセン准教授は、デンマークとグリーンランドにとって今回の合意は、領土を米国に譲らずに約2年に及ぶ対立を終わらせる可能性があるという点で重要だと指摘する。

「トランプ氏には、自分が勝者だと見える形が必要だ」とヤコブセン氏はインタビューで指摘。「だからこそ、圧力をかけた成果だと本人が主張できる新たな合意が必要だった」と述べた。

一方、グリーンランドの取得や政治的な支配というトランプ氏の目標については、「思い通りにはならなかった」と語った。

トランプ氏は18日、ソーシャルメディアへの投稿で合意を発表した。米国の敵対国がグリーンランドに基地を設けたり、軍事拠点を築いたりするのを阻止できるほか、安全保障上の懸念がある投資も阻止できるようになると説明した。

item.title: Sandro Mazzola, famoso delantero del Inter y de la selección italiana, fallece a los 83 años
item.description: El exdelantero de la selección italiana Sandro Mazzola, que pasó los 17 años de su carrera profesional en el Inter de Milán, falleció a los 83 años, informó el club el sábado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El exdelantero de la selección italiana Sandro Mazzola, que pasó los 17 años de su carrera profesional en el Inter de Milán, falleció a los 83 años, informó el club el sábado. Mazzola, considerado un emblema del Inter, marcó 158 goles en 565 partidos, lo que ayudó al equipo a ganar cuatro títulos de la Serie A y dos Copas de Europa. Formó parte de la selección italiana que ganó la Eurocopa de 1968 y llegó a la final del Mundial de México dos años después. "Sandro Mazzola fue uno de los mejores futbolistas de la historia. No solo en la historia de los Nerazzurri", dijo el Inter en un comunicado publicado en su página web oficial, en el que usó el apodo del equipo. "Él era la historia del Inter: se incorporó al club cuando era un niño y nunca lo abandonó". La primera ministra Giorgia Meloni dijo que Italia había perdido a una de las figuras más queridas de su fútbol. "Aportó alegría y pasión a generaciones de italianos, dejando una huella imborrable en nuestra nación", publicó en las redes sociales. Mazzola tenía seis años cuando su padre, Valentino —también internacional con Italia—, falleció en la catástrofe aérea de Superga, un accidente de avión ocurrido en mayo de 1949 en el que pereció toda la plantilla del Torino cuando regresaba de un partido en Lisboa. A los 18 años, Mazzola debutó con el primer equipo cuando el Inter alineó a su equipo juvenil en un partido contra la Juventus, después de que la Federación Italiana revocó una decisión que otorgaba al Inter una victoria por 2-0 tras una invasión del terreno de juego por parte de los aficionados de la Juventus y ordenó la repetición del partido. Mazzola, que de niño había sido mascota del Inter, terminó un examen escolar antes de viajar a Turín, donde marcó el único gol del Inter de penal en la derrota por 9-1 ante la Juventus. Rápidamente se convirtió en titular del primer equipo y ayudó al Inter a ganar su primera Copa de Europa en 1964, al marcar un doblete en la victoria por 3-1 sobre el Real Madrid en la final. Desempeñó un papel clave cuando el Inter volvió a ganar el título la temporada siguiente. Mazzola se retiró en 1977 y más tarde ocupó el cargo de director deportivo del Inter. También llegó a ser director deportivo del Torino, el club de su padre. "La estrella del bigote brilló sobre el terreno de juego, y sigue brillando hoy en día. Como solía decir, tenía un último deseo: ser recordado como un buen hombre, alguien que sigue luchando incluso cuando ganar es imposible, como en aquel 9-1", dijo el Inter.

item.title: Arabie saoudite-Explosions et fumée près de l'aéroport de Ryad après une alerte
item.description: Une importante colonne de fumée était visible samedi près de l'aéroport principal de Ryad après des détonations et des alertes émises pendant la nuit par l'Arabie saoudite pour signaler une potentielle menace autour de la capitale, dans un contexte d'aggravation des attaques menées par les Houthis du Yémen.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Une importante colonne de fumée était visible samedi près de l'aéroport principal de Ryad après des détonations et des alertes émises pendant la nuit par l'Arabie saoudite pour signaler une potentielle menace autour de la capitale, dans un contexte d'aggravation des attaques menées par les Houthis du Yémen. Une vidéo et des photos de Reuters montrent un immense panache de fumée noire s'élevant dans le secteur en question, avec au premier plan l'autoroute menant à l'aéroport, le terminal principal et d'autres installations. Dans cette vidéo, on peut voir des flammes s'élever derrière ce qui semble être des réservoirs de carburant. Le service de presse du gouvernement saoudien n'a fait aucun commentaire dans l'immédiat concernant la fumée et les alertes émises pendant la nuit. La protection civile saoudienne a envoyé ces alertes par téléphone pendant la nuit, faisant état d'un potentiel risque d'attaques aériennes à Ryad et dans la ville d'Al-Kharj, à l'est de la capitale, avant de lever l'alerte samedi dans la matinée. Un journaliste de Reuters présent dans le quartier d'Olaya, à Ryad, a entendu des détonations avant que la levée de l'alerte ne soit annoncée.

item.title: Groenlandia y Dinamarca dicen que el acuerdo con EEUU no supondrá una cesión de soberanía
item.description: Dinamarca y Groenlandia dijeron el sábado que ningún acuerdo con Estados Unidos pondría en peligro la soberanía de Groenlandia, después de que el presidente Donald Trump sostuvo que este le otorgaría a Washington "control permanente" sobre la seguridad de la isla ártica, sin que quedara claro su alcance exacto.
item.dc:creator: Stine Jacobsen, Jacob Grønholt-Pedersen, Tom Little
item.content:encoded: Dinamarca y Groenlandia dijeron el sábado que ningún acuerdo con Estados Unidos pondría en peligro la soberanía de Groenlandia, después de que el presidente Donald Trump sostuvo que este le otorgaría a Washington "control permanente" sobre la seguridad de la isla ártica, sin que quedara claro su alcance exacto. Estados Unidos, Dinamarca y Groenlandia anunciaron a última hora del viernes que habían alcanzado un acuerdo para que Estados Unidos establezca una presencia militar significativa en Groenlandia, a la vez que se prohíbe a los adversarios de Washington construir sus propias bases en la isla. No se han hecho públicos los detalles, entre ellos el grado de presencia militar estadounidense en el territorio danés autónomo ni si se cedería a Washington algún poder formal sobre la política exterior y los recursos. Dinamarca y Groenlandia expresaron su esperanza de que el acuerdo, cuya firma está prevista durante la Asamblea General de la ONU la próxima semana, ponga fin a meses de incertidumbre provocados por las amenazas de Trump de hacerse con el control de Groenlandia. "La próxima semana podría ser una buena semana para Groenlandia, Dinamarca y Estados Unidos", dijo el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores de Dinamarca, Lars Lokke Rasmussen, en un comunicado publicado en Facebook el sábado. "Esperamos que este periodo de incertidumbre dé paso a un acuerdo vinculante que refuerce la seguridad en el Ártico y el Atlántico Norte y, con ello, nuestra seguridad común en el seno de la OTAN y Europa, respetando al mismo tiempo las líneas rojas del Reino (danés)", añadió. Dinamarca y Groenlandia han insistido en repetidas ocasiones en que Washington respete la soberanía del Reino de Dinamarca y acepte que Groenlandia no está en venta. LA VISIÓN DE TRUMP Trump dijo el viernes por la noche en Truth Social que, en virtud de un acuerdo, "Estados Unidos tendrá PARA SIEMPRE plena capacidad para hacer lo que sea necesario en Groenlandia con el fin de garantizar y defender la seguridad de Groenlandia y de los Estados Unidos de América". El acuerdo "otorga a Estados Unidos el control permanente sobre la seguridad y todas las demás necesidades en Groenlandia", señaló Trump, añadiendo que nunca se permitiría a ningún adversario tener una base o presencia militar en Groenlandia, ni realizar inversiones sensibles allí, sin la aprobación expresa por escrito de Washington. Trump hizo el anuncio después de que Reuters informó en exclusiva de que Estados Unidos y Dinamarca estaban a punto de cerrar un acuerdo. "Probablemente este no sea el final de las ambiciones del presidente Trump respecto a Groenlandia y, desde luego, tampoco el final del interés estratégico de Estados Unidos en el territorio y sus recursos", dijo Mikkel Vedby Rasmussen, profesor de ciencias políticas de la Universidad de Copenhague. Si Copenhague cede algún poder formal a Washington, esto plantea en Groenlandia la pregunta de si "esto supone el inicio de la sustitución de la relación colonial con Dinamarca por una relación colonial con Estados Unidos", añadió. El primer ministro de Groenlandia, Jens-Frederik Nielsen, dijo el sábado que estaba satisfecho con el acuerdo propuesto: "El acuerdo reconoce la soberanía y la integridad territorial de nuestro Reino, así como el derecho del pueblo groenlandés a la autodeterminación", dijo en una publicación en Facebook. Un portavoz de la OTAN comunicó el sábado que la alianza acogía con satisfacción el acuerdo, que "contribuiría a promover la seguridad, la estabilidad y la cooperación en esta región vital".

item.title: Russia-backed South Ossetia elects leader close to Moscow
item.description: A former Russian federal official has been elected president of South Ossetia, a Russia-backed breakaway region of Georgia, in a vote Moscow hailed on Saturday as a sign of the territory's desire for closer ties with Moscow.
item.dc:creator: Lucy Papachristou
item.content:encoded: A former Russian federal official has been elected president of South Ossetia, a Russia-backed breakaway region of Georgia, in a vote Moscow hailed on Saturday as a sign of the territory's desire for closer ties with Moscow. Marat Kambolov, the new president, is from North Ossetia, a Russian republic on the other side of the Caucasus mountains from South Ossetia. He has no previous ties to South Ossetia, which broke away from Georgia during the collapse of the Soviet Union in the early 1990s and later secured de facto independence with Russian backing. A brief war between Russia and Georgia in 2008 drove Georgian forces from parts of the territory they had previously controlled. Moscow welcomed Kambolov's victory. "The results demonstrate South Ossetian society's widespread desire for domestic political stability, progress and the comprehensive development of ties with the Russian Federation," the Foreign Ministry said. South Ossetia and Russia signed a treaty in May that deepened cooperation on defence, foreign and security policy and set out plans to integrate energy grids and transport networks. Georgia condemned the treaty as an attempt by Russia to cement its "de facto annexation" of South Ossetia and Abkhazia, another Russia-backed breakaway Georgian region. Tbilisi also criticised Russia's decision to open polling stations in both territories for its [USN:L1N45B029 TEXT:"State Duma election"]s running from September 18 to 20. PUTIN SENDS CONGRATULATIONS The 61-year-old Kambolov previously held senior posts in Russian federal government bodies, including in the education ministry. He was appointed South Ossetia's prime minister in June after Alan Gagloyev stepped down as president to become an adviser to Russian President Vladimir Putin. Putin congratulated Kambolov on Saturday in a telegram published on the Kremlin's website. In a victory speech in the South Ossetian capital Tskhinvali, Kambolov pledged to improve living standards in the region. "We have a great deal of work ahead of us. Only together can we change our republic, our Tskhinvali!" he said. South Ossetia, with a population of about 50,000, is heavily dependent on Russia for food, equipment and energy imports and has little industry of its own. Moscow funds public-sector wages, pensions and major infrastructure projects and operates a military base in the territory. Russian state media said Kambolov won 85% of the vote in Friday's election, with his rivals polling in the single digits. Turnout was 73%.

item.title: Trump Moves to Bar Three News Outlets From White House
item.description: President Donald Trump says he is banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House over coverage he calls “fake news,” though questions remain about how the restrictions would be enforced and whether they could face legal challenges. Bloomberg News White House Correspondent Jeff Mason joins David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend and discusses how this move comes as Trump also faces protests over the future of the Kennedy Center and prepares to address the UN General Assembly with the Iran war expected to be a major focus. item.title: Team performance head Demko banned for 10 years for ethics code breaches
item.description: Ladislav Demko, former head of performance at the UCI Women’s Continental Hess Team, has been banned from all cycling-related activity for 10 years by the International Cycling Union's ethics commission for multiple breaches of its ethics code.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ladislav Demko, former head of performance at the UCI Women’s Continental Hess Team, has been banned from all cycling-related activity for 10 years by the International Cycling Union's ethics commission for multiple breaches of its ethics code. The Ethics Commission, a body independent from the UCI, found that Demko had "fallen short" of the standards required by the ethics code and had abused his position of power. It said an investigation had been opened following complaints from former staff members at Hess Cycling Team and from a rider who was in a consensual relationship with Demko while he was her coach, "concerning allegations of harassment and psychological abuse". Demko had subjected the rider to isolation, humiliation, intimidation and infantilisation, the commission said in a statement. Demko said the accusations stemmed from the frustrations of two staff who had been dismissed by the team. "I am not willing to ruin my savings and have decided to walk away from the world of professional cycling for good," he told Reuters on Saturday. The Slovak said that he had not yet exercised his right to file an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, but would ask for the case to be reopened in the future. He was ordered to pay a fine and the costs of the legal proceedings. The amounts were not disclosed. Hess Cycling Team was founded in 2023 but in August 2025 owner Rolf Hess, a Swiss businessman, announced on Instagram that the team had ceased operations for financial reasons.

item.title: Inside China's AI race
item.description: What does the fight to dominate AI look like from inside China?
item.content:encoded: Follow on Apple or Spotify . Listen on the Reuters app. As the US and China race to dominate artificial intelligence, Reuters correspondents Eduardo Baptista and Laurie Chen say the two countries aren't even playing the same game. On this episode of On Assignment, they take us inside China's AI industry - from Beijing's push to weave AI into every corner of society, to the murky world of chip access, distillation and export controls. Hear what it takes to report on one of the most fast-moving industries on Earth, and why the answer to "who's winning" may depend entirely on how you define the race. item.title: Red Sox ride fast start into rematch vs. Rays
item.description: Boston Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy knows his team has figured out the Tampa Bay Rays pretty well this season.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Boston Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy knows his team has figured out the Tampa Bay Rays pretty well this season. That said, the Red Sox (84-70) still can learn more about the Rays (93-60) when the teams meet Saturday afternoon in St. Petersburg, Fla. "At this point with (the Rays), we've played them enough already," Tracy said. "We have a pretty good understanding of them, (and) they have a pretty good understanding of us. But you could always pick up more stuff." In Friday's series opener, the Red Sox scored four runs over the first three innings and won 4-2 to snap Tampa Bay's six-game winning streak and improve to 6-5 this season vs. the Rays. Boston currently holds the second wild-card position in the American League but is dealing with several injuries. "We have guys beat up that aren't here, and the hope is we get people healthy, and the roster could look even different a week from now than it does right now," Tracy said. Boston's Willson Contreras is day-to-day after getting hit on the hand, while closer Aroldis Chapman (lat tightness) has been unavailable the past two contests. Right-hander Tanner Houck (Tommy John surgery in 2025) and lefty Garrett Crochet (left shoulder inflammation) have advanced in their rehab assignments. Boston left-hander Payton Tolle (9-6, 3.02 ERA) is expected to make his 26th start on Saturday and will try to record his sixth consecutive win. Tolle is 1-0 with an 0.75 ERA over 12 innings in his last two starts, allowing one run on eight hits while striking out 19 with a walk. He is 0-2 with a 4.50 ERA in two starts and one relief outing against Tampa Bay, which already has clinched a playoff berth. Whatever Rays pitching coach Kyle Snyder and the rest of the staff have done with trade-deadline acquisition Freddy Peralta certainly has been a success. Acquired by the club from the New York Mets for three prospects on Aug. 2, Peralta (9-11, 4.67 ERA) -- a right-hander who will start for the Rays on Saturday -- arrived from the Big Apple as a lesser version of what he was during his two All-Star seasons with the Milwaukee Brewers. He was 5-9 with a 4.99 ERA with the Mets, but the work was immediately put in by the Rays to adjust Peralta to where he was when he was a 17-game winner with a sub-3.00 ERA last season. "For some reason, when I got here, when I sat here with Kyle and (bullpen coach Jorge Moncada) and (manager Kevin Cash), they told me, like, 'You're gonna do what you want to do here, and we are going to help you to do it,'" Peralta said. "And we know what you need to do to make those adjustments. We just put everything on the table. I just followed all the instructions, and it's what I am right now." With the Rays, Peralta is 4-2 with a 3.86 ERA in eight starts, but his past four outings have been gems. He has pitched 23 innings and has allowed just two runs on 10 hits, with 17 strikeouts, four walks and an 0.78 ERA in that span. "Fastball Freddy," who is using his changeup much more with the Rays, is 0-2 with a 5.40 ERA in three career starts against Boston. Peralta allowed two runs on three hits in 4 1/3 innings in a 4-0 loss at Boston on July 11 while with the Mets. --Field Level Media

item.title: Japan come from behind to beat Fiji and win Pacific Nations Cup
item.description: Japan pulled off an upset 20-15 victory over Fiji on Saturday to win the Pacific Nations Cup for the first time in seven years, outrunning and overpowering the islanders as they overturned the form book.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Japan pulled off an upset 20-15 victory over Fiji on Saturday to win the Pacific Nations Cup for the first time in seven years, outrunning and overpowering the islanders as they overturned the form book. It was Japan’s fourth win in the competition, which this year also included Canada and the United States, and dethroned Fiji who had won six of the last eight editions. Japan’s three tries at a capacity Chichibunomiya Rugby Stadium in Tokyo all came from mauls, with Mamoru Harada, Ben Gunter and substitute Samisoni Tua going over, while Sam Greene added a conversion and penalty. Fiji, ranked ninth in world rugby to Japan’s 12th spot, scored two tries through Virimi Vakatawa and captain Tevita Ikanivere, with Caleb Muntz adding a conversion and Isaiah Armstrong-Ravula a penalty. Japan’s superior fitness allowed them to play a quick game that tired out the Fijians, who initially looked as if they would prove too physically powerful for their hosts. Vakatawa’s power saw him drive over the line in the 10th minute for the first try of the match despite four Japanese defenders trying to stop him. The 34-year-old former France international was making his second appearance for Fiji after switching his allegiance. Harada had Japan’s first try from a lineout maul in the 22nd minute when Fiji were down to 14 men after a yellow card for prop Mesake Doge, but the favourites went 12-10 ahead at the break after a short pass at the lineout caught out the Japanese defence and saw Ikanivere sprint away to score. Japan dominated the second-half exchanges with Fiji tiring quickly and the hosts had several rolling mauls that Fiji managed to hold off but eventually broke through when Gunter forced his way over in the 57th minute. Armstrong-Ravula’s penalty for Fiji levelled matters at 15-15 with 15 minutes to go, but another maul allowed Tua to score the match-winning try in a major triumph for Japan.

item.title: Reportan humo cerca del aeropuerto de Riad tras alertas en Arabia Saudita
item.description: Una gran columna de humo pudo verse el sábado cerca del principal aeropuerto de Riad, después de que se escucharon explosiones y Arabia Saudita emitió alertas durante la noche advirtiendo de un posible peligro en los alrededores de la capital, en el contexto de una escalada de ataques del grupo hutí de Yemen.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Una gran columna de humo pudo verse el sábado cerca del principal aeropuerto de Riad, después de que se escucharon explosiones y Arabia Saudita emitió alertas durante la noche advirtiendo de un posible peligro en los alrededores de la capital, en el contexto de una escalada de ataques del grupo hutí de Yemen. Las imágenes de vídeo y las fotografías de Reuters mostraban una enorme columna de humo negro elevándose en la zona, con la autopista del aeropuerto, el edificio principal de la terminal y otras instalaciones en primer plano. No hubo comentarios inmediatos de la oficina de prensa del Gobierno saudita en respuesta a las preguntas de Reuters sobre el humo y las alertas nocturnas. La defensa civil saudita envió durante la noche alertas por teléfono sobre un posible peligro en Riad y en la ciudad de Al-Kharj, al este de la capital, antes de dar el "fin de alarma" el sábado por la mañana. Un periodista de Reuters en la zona de Olaya, en Riad, escuchó explosiones antes del "fin de alarma". Si bien este año hubo algunas alertas en Riad tras el inicio de la guerra entre Estados Unidos e Irán, estas fueron las primeras desde que comenzó la escalada con los hutíes en julio. Los hutíes, que controlan las zonas más pobladas de Yemen y gran parte del norte, han estado lanzando ataques contra Arabia Saudita desde que declararon un bloqueo naval contra Riad en julio, con ataques dirigidos contra buques sauditas en el mar Rojo.

item.title: Can India Turn Its Promise Into Prosperity?
item.description: Blackstone COO Jon Gray says India’s young population, expanding middle class and improving infrastructure are drawing interest from global investors. But India’s demographic advantage also creates pressure: millions of young people graduate every year, while formal-sector job creation has not kept pace with their skills and expectations. At the same time, Indian states are competing aggressively for investment by cutting regulatory barriers, building industrial infrastructure and targeting sectors from electronics to semiconductors. The question is whether India can turn its scale, talent and investment momentum into enough productive jobs to sustain its growth. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Phillies turn to improving Andrew Painter in clash vs. Mets
item.description: Christian Scott, Zac Thornton and Nolan McLean are providing the New York Mets hope that they eventually will be part of a rotation for a playoff contender.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Christian Scott, Zac Thornton and Nolan McLean are providing the New York Mets hope that they eventually will be part of a rotation for a playoff contender. The Philadelphia Phillies need rookie Andrew Painter to continue proving that now. Painter will take the mound for the Phillies on Saturday afternoon when they visit the Mets in the third contest of a four-game series between the National League East rivals. Painter (3-9, 5.54 ERA) will oppose Scott (4-5, 3.76) in a battle of right-handers. The Phillies missed a chance to take over sole possession of the top wild-card spot in the NL on Friday night, when Thornton and two relievers combined on a six-hitter in the Mets' 6-3 win. The Phillies, Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres are tied for the NL's three wild-card spots at 85-69. The Cubs lost to the Cincinnati Reds 6-4 before the Padres created the three-way tie hours later with an 8-2 win over the Miami Marlins. The Arizona Diamondbacks reside five games behind the Phillies, Cubs and Padres. The importance of Painter was further magnified Friday, when Philadelphia fell to 0-2 in bullpen games necessitated by the absence of left-hander Jesus Luzardo (shoulder, 15-day injured list). The All-Star was scratched from his scheduled start against the Atlanta Braves last Saturday, when the Phillies used six pitchers as the Braves rolled to a 12-2 win. On Friday, opener Tim Mayza got just one out and allowed three runs while pitching in Luzardo's spot. The Phillies' bullpen also is being taxed by injury and ineffectiveness. Right-hander Jonathan Bowlan departed Thursday's game vs. the Mets with a tight right groin. On Friday, Orion Kerkering gave up Juan Soto's three-run blast in the sixth inning -- the second homer surrendered by Kerkering in his last three outings, during which he has a 13.50 ERA. "Anybody that gives up runs, when things aren't going good, your confidence is not sky high like when you're getting all your outs and everything's going smoothly," Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly said. "But we've got to get past that at this point." Painter is 2-1 with a 3.58 ERA in nine starts since being recalled from Triple-A Lehigh Valley on July 31. He didn't factor into the decision in his most recent start last Sunday, when he gave up one run over five innings as the Phillies beat the Braves 9-4. He has yet to face the Mets in his career. The Mets (70-84) have been under .500 since April and officially were eliminated from playoff contention earlier this week. But McLean and Thornton continued to provide optimism for 2027 by combining to allow just three runs over 12 innings in the first two games of the series. McLean took the hard-luck loss Thursday, when he gave up one run in six innings in the Phillies' 3-0 win. Thornton, McLean and Scott have a combined 3.40 ERA in 66 starts. Thornton and McLean are rookies while Scott is in his second big-league season after Tommy John surgery cut his 2024 campaign short. "I think you have to train like you've never won anything and compete like you've never lost," Mets interim manager Andy Green said Friday night about Thornton. "I think you have to live in that space constantly." Scott took the defeat Sunday after allowing two runs over six innings in the Mets' 2-0 loss to the New York Yankees. He is 1-0 with a 1.80 ERA in two career starts against the Phillies. --Field Level Media

item.title: La France prévoit pour 2026 un déficit de 5,4% et une dette publique à 119,3% du PIB - ministère
item.description: La dette publique de la France devrait atteindre 119,3% du produit intérieur brut (PIB) cette année et pourrait grimper à 121,7% en 2027, a indiqué samedi le ministère de l'Economie et des Finances.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La dette publique de la France devrait atteindre 119,3% du produit intérieur brut (PIB) cette année et pourrait grimper à 121,7% en 2027, a indiqué samedi le ministère de l'Economie et des Finances. Concernant le déficit budgétaire, le ministère dit tabler sur 5,4% du PIB en 2026 et 5,0% en 2027. En 2025, le ratio dette/PIB de la France était de 115,7%. Ces chiffres ont été communiqués au Haut Conseil des finances publiques, l'organisme chargé d'évaluer les prévisions de recettes et de dépenses, dans le projet de budget du gouvernement.

item.title: With playoff hopes flickering, Orioles square off with Brewers again
item.description: There's no sugar-coating the results for the Baltimore Orioles with eight games left in the regular season.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: There's no sugar-coating the results for the Baltimore Orioles with eight games left in the regular season. They stand three games out of the final wild-card spot in the American League and would need to leapfrog three teams to land in the postseason. So they'll try to wipe away the painful result from Friday night in advance of the second game of the three-game series with the visiting Milwaukee Brewers on Saturday afternoon. The Brewers claimed the series opener Friday with a 6-5, 10-inning escape. The Orioles came back from deficits of 3-0 and 5-3 to forge ties, only to lose in the first extra frame. "Losing right now is tough," Baltimore infielder Coby Mayo said. "Obviously, we did a great job rallying back, and you're going to have those games where you rally back and lose. You're going to have the games where you rally back and win." Brewers manager Pat Murphy lauded his team. "We did some good things," he said. "We were fortunate things worked out." Milwaukee (96-58) has baseball's best record and leads the Los Angeles Dodgers by two games in the race for the top seed in the NL playoffs. The Orioles (75-79) had a three-game winning streak snapped even after scoring two runs in the bottom of the ninth to extend Friday's game. "Our guys have shown the resiliency all year and coming back," manager Craig Albernaz said. "We have numerous comebacks and keep on clawing, fighting back. But also we know where we're at right now. We've got to win as many games as we can is an understatement." Murphy has become a fan of the Orioles' energy under Albernaz. "I don't know what place they're in or what place they are in the standings," Murphy said. "But to have those guys playing the way he's got those guys playing and the commitment and the way the fans are into the game, they're playing like a first-place team." Left-hander Robert Gasser (4-5, 4.30 ERA) will start for the Brewers on Saturday. He has a 2.57 ERA in three outings this month and gave up one run in five innings Sunday in his team's 4-3 loss to the Cincinnati Reds. He does not have a decision this month. Gasser has never faced the Orioles in parts of three big-league seasons. Left-hander Trevor Rogers (10-10, 4.22 ERA) will start for the Orioles. He took an 8-1 loss Sunday when he allowed four runs in six innings vs. the Toronto Blue Jays. That followed two strong outings earlier in the month when he gave up a total of three runs covering 14 innings. Rogers has been the winning pitcher in his past three starts at home. In five career starts vs. the Brewers, he's 4-0 with a 2.84 ERA. The Orioles are juggling bullpen possibilities, particularly with right-hander Felix Bautista joining the team in Baltimore at the beginning of the series. It's unclear if he'll be placed on the active roster this weekend, though he has completed an injury rehabilitation assignment in the minor leagues as he works his way back from surgery in August of last season to repair a torn rotator cuff and a torn labrum. Many of the roster decisions are bound to depend on Baltimore's status in the playoff chase. "There's a lot of factors that go into play; that's one of them," Albernaz said. "We try to factor in everything when we make a decision, but more importantly, it's where the player (is) at and how they are feeling. We don't want to force them into anything that they're not comfortable with or physically comfortable with." The Orioles will honor former first baseman/outfielder Trey Mancini (2016-22) before the game. He'll sign a one-day contract with the team to officially retire as an Oriole. Mancini, 34, played in 701 games for Baltimore, batting .270 with 117 homers and 350 RBIs. He played in five games for the Los Angeles Angels this season, hitting .308 with no homers and four RBIs. --Field Level Media

item.title: White Sox eager for bounce-back effort vs. Tigers
item.description: After watching a six-run lead disappear, the Chicago White Sox have little time to regroup in a tightening American League Central race.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: After watching a six-run lead disappear, the Chicago White Sox have little time to regroup in a tightening American League Central race. Chicago will look to bounce back Saturday afternoon when it continues a four-game series against the visiting Detroit Tigers. Saturday's game was moved up from its originally scheduled evening start to 2:10 p.m. ET because of expected inclement weather. The White Sox (78-76) fell one game behind Cleveland after squandering an 8-2 lead in Friday's 11-8 loss to the Tigers. The Guardians (79-75) beat the Athletics 5-3 to take sole possession of first place, although Chicago holds the tiebreaker after winning the season series 7-6. Detroit scored nine unanswered runs, including five in the eighth inning. Hao-Yu Lee tied the game with a two-run homer before Dillon Dingler delivered the go-ahead single and Riley Greene followed with a two-run homer. Lee went 4-for-5 with three RBIs and two runs, while Kevin McGonigle finished 2-for-5 with four RBIs. "I knew there was a chance," Lee told Detroit SportsNet of his game-tying homer. "When I actually saw it go out, I just blacked out. I don't know what I said or did." Detroit (73-81) has won seven of its past nine games. Chicago's offense provided plenty of early support Friday. Colson Montgomery ripped a three-run double during a six-run first inning, while Miguel Vargas hit a two-run homer in the third to match Munetaka Murakami for the team lead with 32. "Yeah, it's tough. No way about it," White Sox manager Will Venable said. "Obviously you have a special first inning there and get the lead. Vargy with a nice homer. Just weren't able to get any outs." Saturday's pitching matchup features Detroit right-hander Jackson Jobe (2-2, 3.89 ERA) against Chicago right-hander Sean Burke (9-7, 3.47). Jobe is coming off his strongest outing of the season. He allowed one run on three hits over a career-high 6 1/3 innings Sunday against the Colorado Rockies, walking one and striking out a career-best eight batters. The White Sox enjoyed considerably more success against Jobe on Aug. 14, tagging him for six runs on nine hits over 3 2/3 innings in a 9-5 Chicago victory. It was Jobe's only appearance against Chicago this season. Jobe is 0-1 with a 6.17 ERA in three career appearances, including two starts, against the White Sox. Burke pitched five innings of relief Monday against Cleveland, allowing one unearned run on four hits with two walks and four strikeouts in Chicago's 7-3 victory. In two starts against Detroit this season, Burke has allowed five runs over 9 2/3 innings. He is 1-0 with a 2.91 ERA in four career starts against the Tigers. Chicago right fielder Tristan Peters is day-to-day with a left shoulder/rib contusion after crashing into the wall while pursuing McGonigle's fifth-inning triple Friday. "I feel all right," Peters said. "We'll see how it feels (on Saturday). Just really sore right now." --Field Level Media

item.title: IMF tells EU ministers AI could boost growth but increase economic strains
item.description: Artificial intelligence could lift European productivity by about 1% over five years, but risks widening inequality, straining power networks and increasing dependence on foreign technology unless governments deepen economic integration, an International Monetary Fund paper said.
item.dc:creator: Jan Strupczewski
item.content:encoded: Artificial intelligence could lift European productivity by about 1% over five years, but risks widening inequality, straining power networks and increasing dependence on foreign technology unless governments deepen economic integration, an International Monetary Fund paper said. The background note, prepared for an informal meeting of European Union finance ministers in Dublin on September 18-19, said the benefits and costs of AI were likely to be distributed unevenly across countries, regions and workers. It said completing the EU single market would help spread AI adoption and its gains more evenly across the 27-nation bloc. The paper echoes concerns raised by former European Central Bank President Mario Draghi and the European Commission that Europe's fragmented capital, labour and energy markets are holding back investment and innovation. The IMF estimated that around 60% of workers in advanced European economies are employed in occupations highly exposed to AI. While some could become more productive through AI tools, others faced displacement as routine tasks become automated, it said, particularly in jobs where AI is more likely to replace labour than complement it. The paper said Europe's data centres already consume roughly 3% of the continent's electricity and that demand would rise sharply as AI use expands. Major technology hubs such as Frankfurt, London, Amsterdam, Paris and Dublin are among the areas most exposed, with data-centre clusters already putting pressure on local power networks. To address that, the EU should invest in cross-border grid infrastructure and deepen integration of the European energy market, the IMF said. The paper also warned that Europe risks developing another strategic dependency because the US and China dominate the development of AI models. It said Europe would need significant investment in its own AI industry to avoid becoming reliant on foreign technology. AI's gains are also likely to be unevenly distributed across and within the EU, the paper said. More advanced economies are expected to benefit disproportionately because they are better prepared for and more exposed to the technology. (This story has been refiled to fix a typo in paragraph 7.)

item.title: Canada optimistic about concluding trade talks with India by year-end, minister says
item.description: Canada is optimistic about concluding negotiations on a comprehensive economic partnership agreement (CEPA) with India by year-end, the country's minister for international trade said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Ira Dugal
item.content:encoded: Canada is optimistic about concluding negotiations on a comprehensive economic partnership agreement (CEPA) with India by year-end, the country's minister for international trade said on Saturday. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney had previously said during a trip to New Delhi in March that the two countries would aim to agree a [USN:L1N3ZQ08U TEXT:"free trade pact"] by the end of the year. "I'm feeling very, very optimistic and energetic that we can get it done in the coming months," Canadian Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu told Reuters in an interview during a visit to India's financial capital Mumbai. Indian trade negotiators are expected to be in Canada next month and leaders from the two countries are likely to meet on the sidelines of the G-20 gathering in December, Sidhu said. One main area of discussion is the energy sector. A Shell-led (SHEL.L) [USN:L6N45913X TEXT:"LNG export facility"] launched in Canada last year and the country has five more projects in various phases of development. "We're having conversations with Indian firms on how they can access those projects, but also how they can invest and secure supply in those projects," Sidhu said, declining to share further details. Beyond liquefied natural gas, both countries are looking to expand cooperation in nuclear energy, where India is looking to significantly [USN:L1N44B0NC TEXT:"boost capacity"]. "Canada has a long history in the nuclear industry, and I do see a lot of benefit for Canadian companies and industries to help build up a supply chain here in India," Sidhu said. Sidhu said, without giving any further details, that a number of large Indian business houses from Reliance Industries (RELI.NS) to Mahindra and Mahindra (MAHM.NS) and the JSW Group are exploring investments in critical mineral projects in Canada as a way to secure supply chains. Companies are looking at ways to make co-investments as supply chains are getting weaponised, he said.

item.title: Porsche could face another 4,000 job cuts, Handelsblatt reports
item.description: Volkswagen's sweeping turnaround plan foresees more than 4,000 further job cuts at Porsche , German business daily Handelsblatt reported on Saturday, following a profit warning linked to problems at the sports car subsidiary.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Volkswagen's sweeping turnaround plan foresees more than 4,000 further job cuts at Porsche (P911_p.DE) , German business daily Handelsblatt reported on Saturday, following a [USN:L1N45A0LS TEXT:"profit warning"] linked to problems at the sports car subsidiary. Files documenting a recent agreement by Volkswagen's supervisory board to usher in the German auto group's [USN:L8N44W0B8 TEXT:"largest restructuring"] yet propose a reduction of "about 4,100 employees" at the brand, addressing an overhead shortfall of some €700 million ($803.8 million), according to Handelsblatt. The newspaper said the cuts would be "in addition to existing agreements". In July, Porsche management and labour representatives [USN:L8N43T10N TEXT:"agreed to"] an additional 5,000 layoffs on top of 4,000 determined earlier, bringing the scope of currently agreed job cuts at the Stuttgart-based 911 maker to around one in five by 2035. Volkswagen declined to comment. A Porsche spokesperson declined to comment on the reported plans of Volkswagen's supervisory board. The parent company can only recommend, but not mandate, such measures at Porsche. Volkswagen on Friday revised down its full-year margin target, now hoping for 1% at best rather than a previous range of 4.0-5.5%. The revision was due in large part to a writedown at Porsche, where CEO Michael Leiters is under pressure to deliver a comeback strategy following a collapse in China sales and a costly reversal of the carmaker's EV strategy. ($1 = 0.8709 euros)

item.title: After deaths of nine women, South Africans gather to run, mourn and demand change
item.description: South Africans gathered for memorial runs and protests this week after the killings of nine women near Johannesburg reignited anger and fear over violence that many say mirrors the dangers women face every day.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Africans gathered for memorial runs and protests this week after the killings of nine women near Johannesburg reignited anger and fear over violence that many say mirrors the dangers women face every day. Police have found the [USN:L8N459116 TEXT:"bodies of nine women"] in Ekurhuleni, east of Johannesburg, over the past two months and are investigating whether the killings are linked. Most of the victims were in their 20s and 30s. Some were found stripped of their clothes and showed signs of sexual assault. A memorial run in Johannesburg on Saturday morning honoured one of the victims, Elizabeth Moselakgomo, who disappeared after going for a run and was found dead days later. Runners lit candles and carried a banner reading: "Enough. Stop Femicide." "We are here because we've lost a runner. But we are not safe anywhere," said Lerato Lentsela, one of dozens of people who dressed in black for the memorial run. "We are not safe running, we are not safe at a post office, we are not safe on a date, we are not safe in our own homes, we are not safe in an Uber." The killings have reignited anger over violence against women in South Africa, where gender-based violence was declared a national disaster in 2025 . Many women say the heightened attention and official promises have done little to make them feel safer. "Enough is enough. Our women deserve to live, walk, run and exist without fear," the Uyinene Mrwetyana Foundation, a charity that campaigns against gender-based violence, said in a statement. President Cyril Ramaphosa said on Thursday that South Africa could not allow itself to grow accustomed to such violence and pledged that no stone would be left unturned in the investigations. But policing in South Africa is weakened by corruption and lack of resources. Only about [USN:L5N3GZ362 TEXT:"one in 10 murders"] is ever solved. "We need to relook at our policing. The only reason these nine women were found was because there was more police presence in the area. This problem is countrywide," said Merlize Jogiat of Women for Change, which held a memorial event in Cape Town on Friday. Some women also criticised police advice urging them to take extra precautions when exercising or walking alone. "Stop placing the responsibility of our safety back onto us," Women for Change said in a social media post. "Women should not have to organise their entire lives around surviving violence and not being next."

FAST

Sept 19 : Aprilia's Jorge Martin made a huge statement in the world championship battle by storming to pole position ahead of title rival and reigning MotoGP champion Marc Marquez of Ducati at the Austrian Grand Prix on Saturday. The 28-year-old Spaniard, the 2024 MotoGP champion, clocked a lap of 1:27.917 in the closing minutes of Q2 at the Red Bull Ring in Spielberg to secure his third pole position of the season, edging Marquez by just 0.015 seconds. Martin will be joined on Sunday's front row by Marquez and KTM's Pedro Acosta, racing at the Austrian manufacturer's home circuit. "I was behind Marc at first," Martin said. "Even though I was fast, I couldn't ride the way I wanted to or brake strong. So I decided to go on my own and avoid the risk of yellow flags. I pushed like crazy. Everything was under control, but definitely on the limit, so I'm really happy.

"It seems like we made a big step from yesterday. I was fast this morning and again in qualifying, so I'm feeling prepared for the race. Marc and Pedro look great as well, so it will be an intense race." Marquez seized the championship lead for the first time this season by winning a chaotic San Marino Grand Prix last weekend. The victory left the 33-year-old Spaniard level with Martin on 274 points but the Ducati rider moved to the top of the standings by virtue of having won more races this season. Martin responded emphatically on Saturday, delivering a blistering lap to deny Marquez pole position. Marquez was upbeat about the outcome though, saying: "Yesterday we were struggling a lot in the time attack, so today we improved. I knew it would be difficult to make the front row but we're here now, so I'm happy. "We know that here it changes a lot between the new tyre and used tyre. The sprint race (later on Saturday) will be one thing but the main race is another, and starting on the front row is always important." Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi, third in the championship standings, qualified fourth, while Trackhouse Aprilia rider Ai Ogura completed the top five.

item.title: Soccer-Villa expose familiar flaws as Tottenham slump continues
item.description: Tottenham Hotspur's £300 million squad rebuild is showing little sign of reviving the club's fortunes after a 3-2 home defeat by Aston Villa left them winless after five Premier League games on ...
item.content:encoded:
Soccer-Villa expose familiar flaws as Tottenham slump continues Reuters | Updated: 19-09-2026 23:07 IST | Created: 19-09-2026 23:07 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Tottenham Hotspur's £300 million squad rebuild is showing little sign of reviving the club's fortunes after a 3-2 home defeat by Aston Villa left them winless after five Premier League games on Saturday. While Villa celebrated their first league win of the season, Tottenham were left staring at another familiar afternoon of frustration as the dark clouds that hung over the club last season returned despite a summer of lavish spending. Roberto De Zerbi's team did finally get on the scoresheet, with late goals from Conor Gallagher and Jan Paul van Hecke, but they came only after a clinical Villa had taken a 3-0 lead. Long-suffering Tottenham fans probably sensed trouble when Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki produced a string of saves early on, and the mood darkened further when Johan Manzambi struck in first-half stoppage time after an error by Andy Robertson. Tottenham were temporarily down to 10 men after Micky van de Ven suffered a facial injury and De Zerbi could not hide his frustration at the manner of the goal. "My focus is why we concede the first goal with 10 players, just for one minute in that situation," the Italian said. "We can stay stronger, we can communicate more and more and more, we can defend in a compact way." Mohammed Kudus thought he had levelled after coming off the bench, but joy turned to despair as the effort was ruled out for offside in the build-up after a VAR check. Any hopes of a comeback were then extinguished when Nicolas Jackson exposed Tottenham's defensive frailties to double Villa's lead before Emi Buendia's superb dipping strike made it 3-0 and sent home supporters streaming for the exits. Tottenham have now won only three of their last 25 Premier League home games, losing 15 of them, and their two points from five matches represent their worst start to a league campaign since 2008 when Juande Ramos was sacked. With an away trip to Manchester United after the international break, the pressure could soon start to ramp up on De Zerbi, who came in seven games from the end of last season and saved the club from relegation. "Today I am very disappointed, very sad and very frustrated for the performance. We can't lose this game in this way, absolutely," he said. The Italian also demanded more from striker Dominic Solanke, who again struggled to make an impact. "We need more from him, for sure, but he's one of my players," De Zerbi said. "He needs to stay better, to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough. He's much better than this Dom Solanke." For Villa, after a turbulent summer of arrivals and departures, there were finally signs that Unai Emery's rebuilt side is beginning to settle. "It's a relief. Leading up to the international break, you don't want to be in the bottom three," captain John McGinn said. "The new players are buying into it, it takes time. It's not easy but it's rewarding."

(This story has not been edited by Devdiscourse staff and is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.title: Russia reports online attacks on electoral system on second day of parliamentary vote
item.description: Russian authorities reported attacks on voting systems and communication lines across the country on Saturday, the second day of a September 18-20 parliamentary election that Moscow is treating as a test of public support for the war in Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russian authorities reported attacks on voting systems and communication lines across the country on Saturday, the second day of a September 18-20 parliamentary election that Moscow is treating as a test of public support for the war in Ukraine . The State Duma election, the first since Russia launched its full-scale war in February 2022, is widely expected to see the ruling pro-Putin United Russia party retain its dominance in Russia's tightly controlled political system. Most anti-war candidates were excluded from the ballot before voting across Russia's 11 time zones got under way, after the Supreme Court ruled last month that the liberal Yabloko party — which wants a ceasefire in Ukraine — had breached electoral rules, something it denied. Some Yabloko candidates, however, are still contesting single-member constituencies, which account for half of the 450 seats in the lower house of parliament. The party has traditionally polled in the single digits. On Saturday authorities said the online voting system in Moscow had been subjected to a strong attack overnight, but said the situation was under control. The attacks were continuing, Central Election Commission (CEC) Chairwoman Ella Pamfilova was cited as saying by state media, but all were being successfully repelled. Russia's digital ministry said it had registered a sabotage attempt on communication lines in the country's Far East, but that the attack had been thwarted and all communication had been restored, state media reported. President Vladimir Putin earlier accused Ukraine of trying to interfere with the vote, without providing evidence. Nationwide turnout as of 1400 local time on Saturday (1100 GMT) stood at 32.58%, according to CEC data cited by state media. In Moldova's separatist pro-Russian Transdniestria region, the election [USN:L8N45B01N TEXT:"triggered a diplomatic dispute"] with Chisinau over its objections to the Kremlin's plan to open 15 polling stations for Russian nationals there. Moscow says the 220,000 residents of Transdniestria, a sliver of land which broke away from Moldova in 1990 at the end of Soviet rule, hold Russian passports and are entitled to vote.

item.title: Greenland, Denmark say Trump deal won't compromise sovereignty
item.description: President Trump said earlier that the deal would give Washington "permanent control" over the Arctic island's security, leaving its precise scope unclear.
item.dc:creator: Stine Jacobsen, Jacob Grønholt-Pedersen, Tom Little
item.content:encoded: Denmark and Greenland on Saturday said any agreement with the United States would not compromise Greenland's sovereignty, after President Donald Trump said the deal would give Washington "permanent control" over the Arctic island's security, leaving its precise scope unclear. The United States, Denmark and Greenland said late on Friday they had reached an [USN:L1N45A0QY TEXT:"agreement"] for the US to develop a significant military presence on Greenland, while prohibiting US adversaries from building their own bases on the island. Key details of the agreement have not been made public, including the scale of US military presence in the self-governing Danish territory and whether any formal power over foreign policy and resources would be ceded to Washington. Denmark and Greenland expressed hope that a deal, which is expected to be signed during the UN General Assembly next week, would end months of uncertainty triggered by [USN:L8N4051Z5 TEXT:"Trump's threats"] to seize control of Greenland. "Next week could be a good week - for Greenland, Denmark, and the United States," Denmark's Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen said in a statement posted on Facebook on Saturday. "A time of uncertainty will hopefully give way to a binding agreement that strengthens security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic, and thereby our shared security within NATO and Europe - while respecting the (Danish) Kingdom's red lines," he said. But some residents in Greenland's capital Nuuk expressed scepticism about closer ties with Washington. "The US should not control Greenland. I think it’s better if we have cooperation with NATO," said Jakob Ludvigsen, 65. "Trump should stay far, far, far away from Greenland," Marianne Hansen, a 71-year-old retired chef, told Reuters in Nuuk. "He should not expect our children and grandchildren to become Americans in the future." Denmark and Greenland have repeatedly insisted that Washington respect the sovereignty of the Danish kingdom and accept that Greenland is not for sale. TRUMP'S VISION FOR GREENLAND DEAL Trump said on Truth Social on Friday that under a deal, "the United States will FOREVER have the complete ability to do what is necessary in Greenland in order to secure and defend the security of Greenland, and the United States of America." The deal "gives the United States permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland," Trump said, adding that no adversary would ever be permitted to have a base or military presence in Greenland, or make sensitive investments there, without Washington's express written approval. Trump made the announcement after Reuters exclusively reported that the US and Denmark were closing in on a deal. "This is probably not the end of President Trump's ambitions for Greenland and certainly not the end of US strategic interest in the territory and its resources," said Mikkel Vedby Rasmussen, a political science professor at the University of Copenhagen. If Copenhagen cedes any formal authority to Washington, it raises the question in Greenland of whether "this is the beginning of replacing the colonial relationship with Denmark with a colonial relationship to the United States," he said. Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen said in a Facebook post on Saturday that the proposed deal "recognizes the sovereignty and territorial integrity of our Kingdom and the right of the Greenlandic people to self-determination." Trump's threats, which peaked in January, triggered a diplomatic crisis that strained relations within NATO and pushed Denmark and Greenland into [USN:L6N3YM156 TEXT:"negotiations"] aimed at defusing the pressure. A NATO spokesperson on Saturday said the alliance welcomed the agreement, which would "help advance security, stability and cooperation in this vital region."
